newsitem.title: LATVIA: POTENTIAL INVESTORS AGAINST LATVENERGO SPLIT.
newsitem.headline: POTENTIAL INVESTORS AGAINST LATVENERGO SPLIT.

text.p: Electricity company Latvenergo, said on Friday that potential German investors, including Preussen Electra, advised against the planned Latvenergo split into smaller companies.
The company said in a statement that Preussen and Bewag were of the opinion that during its sell-off Latvenergo should not be split into several small companies.
"In the big and international European electricity market small energy companies would not be able to withstand competition," the statement said, quoting the German companies.
"The restructuring of the company should be carried out after privatisation is complete, the potential investors consider," the statement added.
Under the current sell-off plan, Latvenergo would be turned into a holding company by January 1998, splitting off four power-generating companies and the grid as separate entities.
